name: 142. Tool-result cache marker survives translation to gpt-5.6 function_call_output (tool-result cache breakpoint)
description: Claude Code places its per-turn cache_control marker on the last block of the conversation, which is a tool_result after every tool call. The Anthropic converter carries that marker on the function_call_output item; the OpenAI Responses converter used to translate only input_text blocks, so the marker was stripped and the tool body flattened to a plain string: no prompt_cache_breakpoint, no explicit mode, and caching stopped after the first tool turn on gpt-5.6 / gpt-6. The fix marks the function_call_output content part (OpenAI documents prompt_cache_breakpoint there) and keeps the output in array form. Case 1 pins that the request stays in implicit mode: explicit-only mode checks only the breakpoints in the current request, so Claude Code's rolling marker never read the previous turn back. The rolling-marker cases send two Claude Code turns on OpenAI, the Bedrock runtime OpenAI endpoint (bedrock_openai_ep; plain bedrock sends a cross-region id through Converse and never reaches this converter) and Bedrock Mantle; turn 2 must read the turn-1 prefix back. Turn 1 sets a collection variable that turn 2 reads, so a filtered or rerun selection of turn 2 brings its turn 1 along. Case 2 pins the Claude Code shape through the drop-in messages route: system and tool_result both marked, so the cold write must extend past the 2000-token tool result (a write pinned at the system prefix is the pre-fix signature). The prompt cache mode comparison cases send one Claude Code conversation twice: once with prompt_cache_options.mode explicit through x-bf-passthrough-extra-params, once in the default implicit mode. The explicit arm must read turn 1's system prefix back, which needs all four turn-2 markers kept (the passthrough mode, not only the typed field, decides the ceiling), and the implicit arm must read more than the explicit arm. Case 3 pins the Chat Completions path, where cache_control on text parts is now translated too: the caller asks for explicit mode, so a stripped marker means no breakpoint and no write at all.

item.name: openai gpt-5.6-sol native responses: cache_control on function_call_output keeps implicit mode - tool-result cache breakpoint

exec: pm.test('tool-result marker does not switch the request to explicit-only caching', function(){ var mode = j.prompt_cache_options && j.prompt_cache_options.mode; pm.expect(mode, 'prompt_cache_options.mode explicit drops the implicit lookback over earlier messages: ' + pm.response.text()).to.not.eql('explicit'); });

item.name: openai gpt-5.6-sol drop-in messages route: Claude Code shaped tool_result cache_control writes the whole conversation - tool-result cache breakpoint

exec: // The system prefix is ~5900 tokens and the tool_result ~2000. With the breakpoint on the tool_result the explicit cache write must cover both; a write anchored before the tool_result (marker dropped) stays under 7000.

pm.test('cold cache write extends past the tool_result (cache_creation_input_tokens > 7000)', function(){ var w = (j.usage && j.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens) || 0; pm.expect(w, 'cache_creation_input_tokens: ' + pm.response.text()).to.be.above(7000); });

item.name: openai gpt-5.6-sol native chat completions: cache_control on system and tool text parts becomes prompt_cache_breakpoint under explicit mode - tool-result cache breakpoint

exec: // The caller asked for explicit mode. With the markers translated the cold write covers the ~5900-token system prefix plus the ~2000-token tool result; with them stripped, explicit mode has no breakpoint and OpenAI caches nothing.

pm.test('cold cache write covers system prefix and tool result (cache write tokens > 7000)', function(){ var d = (j.usage && j.usage.prompt_tokens_details) || {}; var w = (typeof d.cached_write_tokens === 'number' ? d.cached_write_tokens : 0) || (typeof d.cache_write_tokens === 'number' ? d.cache_write_tokens : 0); pm.expect(w, 'cache write tokens: ' + pm.response.text()).to.be.above(7000); });

item.name: openai gpt-5.6-sol drop-in messages route: Claude Code rolling tool_result marker, turn 1 - claude code rolling marker

exec: // Turn 2 reads this back, which links the pair for filter-collection.mjs: a sliced or --rerun-failed selection of turn 2 pulls this request in, so the cache is warm in the same newman process.

item.name: openai gpt-5.6-sol drop-in messages route: Claude Code rolling tool_result marker, turn 2 reads turn 1 back - claude code rolling marker

exec: pm.test('turn 1 ran in this newman process', function(){ pm.expect(pm.collectionVariables.get('rollingMarker_openai_t1'), 'turn 1 did not warm the cache in this run, so a cache miss here says nothing about the fix').to.eql('warm'); });

// Claude Code moves its single conversation marker to the newest tool_result every turn. The ~5900-token system prefix plus the ~2000-token first tool_result were cached by turn 1; turn 2's marker sits on a new tool_result. Implicit mode looks back over earlier message endings and reads the turn-1 prefix (> 7000). Forced explicit-only mode checks only this request's breakpoints, so it reads back just the system prefix (< 7000) and rewrites the rest.

pm.test('turn 2 reads the previous turn back from cache (cache_read_input_tokens > 7000)', function(){ var r = (j.usage && j.usage.cache_read_input_tokens) || 0; pm.expect(r, 'cache_read_input_tokens (about 5900 means only the system prefix was reused): ' + pm.response.text()).to.be.above(7000); });

item.name: openai gpt-5.6-sol drop-in messages route: Claude Code cached tokens, passthrough explicit mode arm, turn 2 - prompt cache mode comparison

exec: pm.test('turn 1 ran in this newman process', function(){ pm.expect(pm.collectionVariables.get('pcModeCompare_explicit_openai_t1'), 'turn 1 did not warm the cache in this run').to.eql('warm'); });

// The caller sets prompt_cache_options.mode explicit through x-bf-passthrough-extra-params, so the wire request is explicit-only and the only readable entry is turn 1's system block 1 prefix (~5900 tokens). Turn 2 sends four markers. Bifrost must keep all four, because explicit mode has no implicit breakpoint to leave a slot for. A ceiling that ignores the passthrough mode keeps three and drops system block 1, the earliest, so nothing matches and the read is 0.

pm.test('passthrough explicit mode keeps the earliest breakpoint (cache_read_input_tokens > 5000)', function(){ pm.expect(read, 'cache_read_input_tokens (0 means system block 1 was dropped from the explicit request): ' + pm.response.text()).to.be.above(5000); });

item.name: openai gpt-5.6-sol drop-in messages route: Claude Code cached tokens, implicit mode arm, turn 2 - prompt cache mode comparison

exec: pm.test('turn 1 ran in this newman process', function(){ pm.expect(pm.collectionVariables.get('pcModeCompare_implicit_openai_t1'), 'turn 1 did not warm the cache in this run').to.eql('warm'); });

// Same two turns as the explicit arm, without prompt_cache_options. Implicit mode looks back over earlier message endings, so turn 2 reads turn 1's whole prompt (system plus the ~2000-token tool result), not just the system prefix.
pm.test('implicit mode reads the previous turn back (cache_read_input_tokens > 7000)', function(){ pm.expect(read, 'cache_read_input_tokens: ' + pm.response.text()).to.be.above(7000); });

// The comparison the fix rests on: for the same conversation, implicit mode must cache more than explicit-only mode. If it does not, keeping the default mode stops being the better choice for Claude Code traffic.

pm.test('implicit mode reads more than explicit-only mode for the same conversation', function(){ pm.expect(explicitRead, 'the explicit arm did not record its cache read in this run').to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(read, 'implicit read ' + read + ' vs explicit read ' + explicitRead).to.be.above(Number(explicitRead)); });
